question_text: Two clients read version7 of a database row. One commits a change, creating version8. Outline how comparing the saved version before the second update can prevent a lost update.
adaptation_rationale: Original timestamp ordering is narrowed to a supplied version-check mechanism illustrating transaction consistency/isolation; no particular timestamp protocol is required.
solution: The database compares the second client’s saved version7 with current version8. It rejects or retries the stale update rather than overwriting the newer committed data.
